author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner can cancel an upcoming visit from the owner detail page
summary: The owner detail page offers a cancel action beside each upcoming visit (date later than today). Cancelling permanently removes that visit from the pet's record; past visits are historical and show no cancel action.
acceptance_criteria: Given a pet with an upcoming visit (date later than today), when the owner detail page is shown, then a cancel action appears beside that visit.
Given a pet with a past visit (date today or earlier), when the owner detail page is shown, then no cancel action appears beside that visit.

Given an upcoming visit, when its cancel action is invoked, then the visit is removed from the pet's record and the owner detail page shown afterward no longer lists it, while the pet's other visits remain.
Given a request to cancel a visit that does not belong to the named owner's pet, when it is submitted, then it is refused.

Given a request to cancel a visit whose date is today or earlier, when it is submitted, then it is refused — the cancel path guards the upcoming-visit boundary rather than trusting the page to have hidden the action.
non_goals: Amending or rescheduling a booked visit (NG-5) — only cancellation is in scope
Retaining a cancelled visit in a cancelled state — the record is removed, not flagged
Deleting an owner or a pet (NG-4)
notes: Upcoming = visit date strictly later than today, matching the booking boundary in REQ-VIS-001. 'Removes from the pet's record' means permanent removal through the Owner aggregate: there is no VisitRepository and Pet holds visits via @OneToMany(cascade=ALL) with orphanRemoval NOT currently set — system-design-expert must resolve the concrete delete path. This request reverses the cancel portion of NG-4/NG-5, which have been narrowed accordingly.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Routine mutation through the documented Owner-aggregate write path (system-design.md Overview + Contracts 'Invariants the rows cannot carry'): there is no VisitRepository, so cancellation is a removal from the aggregate persisted by OwnerRepository.save(owner), mirroring the booking write in VisitController.processNewVisitForm (VisitController.java:97-112). The one adjustment to an existing pattern is the Pet.visits mapping. It is @OneToMany(cascade=ALL) WITHOUT orphanRemoval, and visits.pet_id is nullable (verified via Read: db/h2/schema.sql:58-64, Pet.java:56). Removing a Visit from pet.getVisits() and saving therefore issues UPDATE visits SET pet_id=NULL (dissociation, orphan row left behind), NOT a DELETE, and would fail the PRD's 'permanently removes' requirement. Resolution: add orphanRemoval=true to Pet.visits so the same aggregate save cascades a DELETE. An explicit delete is foreclosed because a VisitRepository would breach the documented no-repository-for-Pet/Visit invariant; orphan removal keeps the single OwnerRepository write path intact.
integration_points: New route POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/cancel on VisitController. HTML forms are GET/POST only and no HiddenHttpMethodFilter is configured, so POST is used, consistent with every existing mutation. The URL verb 'cancel' follows the ubiquitous-language term (which rejects 'delete').
ownerDetails.html visit loop (lines 67-70) gains a cancel control rendered only when the visit is upcoming (visit.date strictly after today), matching the server-side guard.
Redirect target redirect:/owners/{ownerId} reuses the booking flow's post-write redirect; the template already renders ${message}/${error} flash slots for the outcome.

patterns.description: Existing aggregate write: load Owner by ownerId, mutate via owner.addVisit, owners.save(owner), redirect:/owners/{ownerId}. The cancel handler mirrors this shape; reuse the loadPetWithVisit-style owner/pet resolution for ownership.

Aggregate traversal + mutation methods. Add a symmetric removal (e.g. a Pet.removeVisit or Owner.removeVisit(petId,visitId)) that locates the visit by id within the pet and detaches it from pet.getVisits().

Server-side upcoming-boundary check (!date.isAfter(now)) used by booking. The cancel guard reuses the same boundary to refuse a visit dated today or earlier. Guard placement in the controller follows current convention; Open Question #2 (business rules in controllers) is not in scope for this slice.

risks.risk: Without orphanRemoval the removal silently orphans the visit row (pet_id NULL) rather than deleting it. An assertion that only reads the returned Owner graph would pass while a dangling DB row remains.
risks.mitigation: Add orphanRemoval=true to Pet.visits; assert post-cancel absence at the persisted level (re-fetch the owner) not only on the in-memory collection.

risks.risk: A new user-facing label key for the cancel control breaks the REQ-LANG-002 build-time bundle-parity test if it is not present in every locale bundle.
risks.mitigation: Add the key to all messages_*.properties (eleven locales) as part of the slice.

risks.risk: Ownership and upcoming guards must hold server-side independent of the template hiding the action (acceptance criteria 4 and 5).
risks.mitigation: Controller resolves owner->pet via owner.getPet(petId) (already throws for a foreign pet), then locates the visit within pet.getVisits() by id (absent => refuse), then applies the isAfter(now) boundary before any mutation. A foreign-pet or missing-visit request is refused the same way the existing loadPetWithVisit refuses a mismatched pet.

notes: Delete-path resolution (the PRD's explicit question): orphan removal on Pet.visits, NOT an explicit delete and NOT a new VisitRepository (the latter breaches the documented aggregate-root invariant). The Owner aggregate owns the operation; persistence reaches the DB through the existing OwnerRepository.save(owner) with cascade+orphanRemoval issuing the DELETE. HTTP shape: POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/cancel, redirect:/owners/{ownerId}. Ownership enforced by aggregate traversal (owner->pet->visit); upcoming guard by visit.getDate().isAfter(LocalDate.now()) mirroring booking. ADR considered and declined: the choice is forced by the existing no-repository invariant, is reversible (an annotation flag), and is not a genuinely open trade-off. No system-design.md write now: its provenance is strict current-state (derived-from-code); doc-sync should extend the Contracts 'Invariants the rows cannot carry' note to record that a visit is removed from the aggregate by orphan removal and wire REQ-VIS-003 into the Implements column of Owner/Pet/VisitController/OwnerRepository once the code lands. Oracle N/A here (IntelliJ not connected this run; Java-only oracle cannot see JPA-mapping/schema evidence) - verified via Read of Pet.java:56, Visit.java, db/h2/schema.sql:58-64, VisitController.java. No design-doc-autofix records to audit.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: The new POST .../visits/{visitId}/cancel endpoint permanently deletes a row, but the application has no Spring Security on the classpath, so no CSRF token protects any mutation. POST is the correct verb (avoids GET prefetch/caching/link-triggered deletion) and the gap is pre-existing and app-wide (shared by visit booking and owner/pet edit), not introduced by this slice. However, adding a destructive delete endpoint raises the practical impact of the existing tokenless posture: a forged cross-site POST could now force-delete a victim's upcoming visits. Deciding whether to add Spring Security / CSRF protection is an architectural, human-owned call — flagged for awareness, not blocking this slice.

orphanRemoval=true does not widen blast radius: removeVisit is called only in the new cancel path (grep-confirmed), no existing write path removes a visit, and visits are eagerly fetched so the persisted collection is complete on save
No XSS in ownerDetails.html cancel control: th:action interpolates only integer ids and the label is a #{cancelVisit} bundle key, both Thymeleaf auto-escaped

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Supersedes the line-5 design-block to resolve the two clarify findings. Delete-path resolution is unchanged (orphanRemoval on Pet.visits, no VisitRepository, persisted through OwnerRepository.save(owner)). This revision binds the REFUSAL MECHANISM, which the prior block left implicit, and records the now-landed code into system-design.md (finding 2, already applied to docs/system-design.md lines 80/89/90/93/97).
integration_points: Refusal mechanism is SPLIT by refusal kind, because the two guards refuse two different things. GUARD A (ownership / not-found): owner.getPet(petId) for a foreign pet, and findVisit(pet,visitId) for a visit id absent from the owner's own pet, are integrity violations against a resource that is not the named owner's. Keep the existing IllegalArgumentException treatment UNCHANGED: it is the same class of precondition failure that loadPetWithVisit / owner.getPet already throw for across the codebase, the security-reviewer approved this ownership enforcement, and no other controller maps these to a bespoke 4xx. Expected HTTP outcome: the framework's default mapping (HTTP 500 error page). Acceptance criterion 4 ('refused') is met because no mutation occurs. A forged/stale/foreign id is not a normal user action, so an error page is the acceptable and consistent outcome; a codebase-wide integrity-violation-to-404 mapping is a separate cross-cutting concern, out of this slice's scope.

GUARD B (past-date / not-upcoming): the visit exists and belongs to the owner's pet, but its date is today or earlier. This is a BUSINESS-RULE refusal — a legitimate owner acting on a stale page whose cancel action should have been hidden. It must NOT 500. Redirect-with-flash: return "redirect:/owners/{ownerId}" and set redirectAttributes.addFlashAttribute("error", <message>) BEFORE returning; do NOT throw. Expected HTTP outcome: HTTP 302 to /owners/{ownerId}, which then renders the existing alert-danger #error-message banner (ownerDetails.html:13-14). No mutation occurs.

Flash contract: attribute name is 'error' (the ${error} slot already rendered at ownerDetails.html:13-14), value is a literal English string — matching the established controller convention (OwnerController.java:80,148,154 all use addFlashAttribute("error", "<literal>")). Do NOT introduce a message-bundle key for the flash string: no controller flash message uses one, and REQ-LANG-002 governs templates/bundles, not controller-set flash text. Suggested message: 'The visit could not be cancelled because it is no longer upcoming.' (wording may be tuned to match the codebase's terse style; keep it non-leaky and user-facing).

patterns.description: Established business-rule refusal UX: redirect to the detail page with addFlashAttribute("error", <literal English string>), rendered by the ${error} alert-danger slot. Guard B mirrors this exactly.
Established integrity-violation treatment: an owner/pet/visit id that does not resolve within the aggregate throws IllegalArgumentException. Guard A keeps this unchanged.

risks.risk: Restructuring processCancelVisitForm could accidentally leave the past-date guard on the throw path, or move the flash-set after the return, yielding a 500 or a lost banner for guard B.
risks.mitigation: In the handler: findVisit(pet,visitId) first (guard A stays a throw); then if date is null or not isAfter(now), set the 'error' flash attribute and return redirect:/owners/{ownerId} WITHOUT throwing and WITHOUT saving; only past both guards do pet.removeVisit(visit) + owners.save(owner) + 'message' flash.

risks.risk: Tests must be updated to the split outcomes.
risks.mitigation: shouldRefuseCancellingPastVisit asserts status 3xx redirect to /owners/{ownerId}, flash attribute 'error' present, and the visit still persisted (no mutation) — NOT an exception/500. shouldRefuseCancellingVisitNotBelongingToOwnersPet asserts refusal via the existing integrity-violation path (no mutation), the same way the booking tests assert loadPetWithVisit's foreign-pet refusal.

notes: Finding 1 (code-quality-reviewer, VisitController.java:129) RESOLVED: refusal mechanism split by kind — guard A (ownership/not-found) keeps the existing IllegalArgumentException/500 integrity-violation path; guard B (past-date business-rule refusal) becomes 302 redirect:/owners/{ownerId} + addFlashAttribute("error", literal). This is a single binding source for the implementer. Finding 2 (doc-reviewer, docs/system-design.md:97) RESOLVED: the provenance objection lapsed once the code landed in the working tree, so the deferred edits are applied now — VisitController row description extended and REQ-VIS-003 added to Implements for Owner (l.89), Pet (l.90), OwnerRepository (l.93), VisitController (l.97); the line-80 Invariants note extended to record the orphan-removal removal path. Descriptions for Owner/Pet were lightly extended for accuracy (cancellation entry point; orphan-removal delete). Visit's own row (l.92) left unchanged per the reviewer's list. No ADR: the refusal split reuses two established codebase patterns (redirect-with-error-flash for business-rule refusal; throw for integrity violation) and introduces no new trade-off. No design-doc-autofix records to audit. Oracle N/A this run (IntelliJ not connected; the load-bearing evidence is the Thymeleaf flash slots and controller flash-string convention, verified via Read/Grep of ownerDetails.html and OwnerController.java).

findings.description: New test method shouldDeleteVisitRowWhenRemovedFromPetAggregate does not follow the BDD naming school (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}) that applies to all new tests written from 2026-07-31 onward per testing-principles.md §Test Naming.

New test uses bare integer literals findById(6) and getPet(7) referencing seed data without tier-1 or tier-2 names. The three-tier convention eliminates mystery literals; a new test writes behind named constants from the start per testing-principles.md §Three-Tier Data Naming Convention.
findings.fix: Extract class-level named constants, e.g. private static final int OWNER_WITH_PETS_AND_VISITS = 6; and private static final int PET_WITH_TWO_VISITS = 7; and replace the bare literals.

findings.description: All five new test methods use the should... prefix without the required the prefix, violating the BDD school (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}) that applies to all new tests written from 2026-07-31 onward per testing-principles.md §Test Naming.

The refusal tests assert hasRootCauseInstanceOf(IllegalArgumentException.class) rather than an HTTP response. This tests the internal exception type that escapes MockMvc — an implementation detail — not the HTTP-observable behavior a real client sees. Adding proper @ExceptionHandler for IllegalArgumentException (the correct production improvement, which would return a 4xx response) would cause assertThatThrownBy to fail because no exception would escape, breaking the test while the behavior is correct. The right assertion shape is mockMvc.perform(...).andExpect(status().is4xxClientError()) or a redirect with an error flash. The verify(owners, never()).save(any()) checks are acceptable as secondary confirmations that no side effect occurred, and the mocking policy (Mockito tolerated on this pre-existing @MockitoBean class) is respected — the fault is solely with the exception-assertion pattern.

The PRD acceptance criterion 5 reads: given a visit whose date is today or earlier, the cancel is refused. The shouldRefuseCancellingPastVisit test uses LocalDate.now().minusDays(1) (yesterday) but does not test LocalDate.now() (today). The today boundary is explicitly stated in the acceptance criteria and in the server-side guard (!visit.getDate().isAfter(LocalDate.now())), where today satisfies the condition. A dedicated test asserting refusal when visitDate equals LocalDate.now() is required to cover this boundary.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Ownership/IDOR enforcement survives the refusal-split refactor and remains un-bypassable: loadPetWithVisit binds the model Owner to path ownerId (owners.findById) and scopes pet to owner.getPet(petId); findVisit filters only that pet.getVisits() by id. Guard B (date check + redirect-with-error-flash) executes only AFTER findVisit returns, so the redirect path cannot be reached for any visit that is not the named owner-pet-aggregate member. A foreign or nonexistent visitId hits findVisit orElseThrow (guard A) first.

Guard ordering leaks no existence of another owner data: findVisit searches only this pet visits, so a globally-existing-but-foreign visit and a wholly nonexistent visit both fall through to the same orElseThrow / same 500. No response differential to use as an existence oracle.

New guard-B flash path discloses nothing: the error flash value is a fixed literal English string (no visit id, date, description, or owner data), and it is rendered through the auto-escaping th:text=${error} slot at ownerDetails.html:14. No reflected or stored XSS and no data leakage introduced.

Upcoming-visit guard is genuinely server-side: !visit.getDate().isAfter(LocalDate.now()) (with an explicit null-date branch) is evaluated in processCancelVisitForm before any mutation, independent of the templates th:if hiding of the cancel form; the today boundary refuses as specified.

No mutation occurs on either refusal path: neither guard A (throw) nor guard B (redirect) calls owners.save; the pre-guard pet.removeVisit(stagedVisit) only drops the transient blank Visit staged by loadPetWithVisit in memory and is never persisted on a refusal. Only past both guards does pet.removeVisit(visit)+owners.save(owner) run.

Pre-existing tokenless-POST/CSRF exposure of the destructive cancel endpoint is unchanged by this refactor (guard B moving from throw to 302 redirect does not alter the mutation path or its reachability); the escalation remains with the human per .scratch/escalations.md and is not re-raised.
